title.narrative: Improve access to lifesaving preventive nutrition specific intervention for girls and boys aged 6-59 months and Plws in Daraa

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgt In 2023, Daraa governorate is witnessing an alarming rise in wasting and stunting among children under five, driven by inadequate diets for this age group, The prevalence of Global Acute Malnutrition (GAM) has surged threefold in the past five years, escalating from 1.1 per cent in 2019 to 3.4 per cent in 2023 across Daraa governorate (SMART,2023). The burden of wasting in children under-five has surged by 40 per cent in 2023 compared to 2019, with 13,963 children urgently requiring life-saving treatment for Acute Malnutrition. Of this group, 6,981 children grapple with severe wasting, presenting a significantly heightened risk of mortality. Stunting rates have consistently risen across Daraa governorate from 12.3 per cent in 2019 to 15.8 per cent in 2023. Furthermore, extreme poverty affected more than 1 in 4 Syrians, while it had been virtually nonexistent in 2009. This situation has weakened the ability of caregivers to provide nutritious diets to the most vulnerable children thus increasing their risk to malnutrition and death. Consequently, nearly 7 out of 10 children aged 6 to 23 months live in child food poverty meaning that they are fed fewer than the recommended 5 out of 8 food groups in a day to stand a chance of attaining optimal growth and development.ltbrgtAl Bir Daraa NGO has an ongoing agreement with UNICEF's Health and Nutrition program to enhance access to primary health care and nutrition services for vulnerable girls, boys, and women of childbearing age across Daraa governorate. To complement existing UNICEF-supported services and ensure that vulnerable children and pregnant or lactating women receive a diverse, nutritious diet, the NGO plans to provide Cash for Nutrition assistance to families with children aged 6-59 months and PLWs those with acute wasting.ltbrgtTo address the vulnerability of households with children aged 6-59 months and PLWs suffering from malnutrition in Daraa district, AlBir NGO will provide cash assistance for nutrition based on the following criteria: 1) households with at least one wasted child aged 6-23 months( admitted,discharged) , and 2) households with at least one wasted PLW ltbrgtadmitted,discharged). Each household will receive 12 rounds of cash assistance, totaling 40 USD per month. Cases of malnutrition are identified and registered or to be identified through UNICEF-supported clinics and outreach teams.ltbrgtThe grant will offer cash assistance for nutrition to 570 families (2,850 individuals) at high risk of malnutrition in prioritized areas of Daraa governorate, as outlined in the SHF allocation strategy. During regular visits to UNICEF-supported fixed and mobile clinics, clear messages will communicate the purpose of the cash—providing nutrition to procure healthy food and safeguard mothers and children from malnutrition.ltbrgtThe proposed project is in line with Nutrition sector Humanitarian response plan 2023-2024 sector objective1) Improved access and quality to lifesaving preventive nutrition specific and sensitive interventions for children (girls and boys) under five years of age, pregnant and lactating women Output indicators: 1.8. Number of children 6 – 23 months receiving BSFP (Nutrition CVA), and 1.9. Number of PLWs receiving Nutrition CVA for nutrition outcomes (BSFP)ltbrgtlt/pgt
